newsitem.title: UK: Actress Goldie Hawn takes elephant to Harrods sale.
newsitem.headline: Actress Goldie Hawn takes elephant to Harrods sale.

text.p: Shoppers took planes, trains, and cars to the opening of a sale at the prestigious London department store Harrods on Wednesday, but actress Goldie Hawn chose a different form of transport -- a giant fake elephant.
Hawn, clad in an ankle-length coat and a body-hugging blue dress, rode a life-size replica of an Indian elephant on wheels to the store to open the doors on its famed January sale.
The American celebrity made the trip to London to accept a $25,000 donation from Harrods chairman Mohamed Al Fayed for Fauna and Flora International, a charity that works to protect Asian elephants.

"I've always loved elephants, and I've never really understood why. But whatever it was, it's made a big dent in my life, and it's given me the opportunity to reach out and do something for them," Hawn told a news conference.
Thousands of bargain-hunters -- including some who had waited in the cold for over four hours -- stampeded into the store to take advantage of steep discounts on pricey items.
Hawn also sampled some of the goods, trying on a 300,000 pound ($500,000) emerald and diamond necklace (reduced from 600,000 pounds) before moving on for more browsing.
Harrods said it sold 800,000 pounds worth of goods in the first hour after the 0900 GMT opening, up about 10 percent versus the same period last year.
The store, located in chic Knightsbridge, said it expected turnover to hit a peak on Saturday, when Harrods will offer additional discounts for account holders.
The store expected to beat last year's one-day sales record of 13 million pounds, set on the first Saturday of the sale.
"It does look as if we will, but we don't want to count our chickens before they're hatched," Harrods spokesman Michael Cole told Reuters. ($1=.5922 Pound)
